transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, my head has just been feeling a little foggy lately. It's probably nothing major, but I've been making a few little mistakes in my client notes at work, and sometimes I just completely forget what I was about to do. I'm a personal care aide, so I always try to be really careful and do a good job, and this just isn't like me at all. 

I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out. I hope it's okay that I came in for something like that?
How long have you been noticing this mental fogginess and forgetfulness—did it come on gradually over weeks or months, or has it always been somewhat present since childhood?

Oh, no, definitely not since childhood. I've always prided myself on being really organized—I promise I'm usually very good at my job and staying on top of things. I wouldn't want you to think I've always been this scatterbrained. 

Um, it hasn't been going on for months, either. It's actually pretty recent. This whole shift really just started... well, about two weeks ago. My, um... my uncle passed away, and it kind of started right after that. 

I hope it's okay that I mentioned that? I know you're asking about my memory and not my family, I just... I thought it might be helpful for you to know, if that makes sense?
Since your uncle passed away, have you been feeling sad, down, or emotionally heavy most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, yeah... I guess I have been. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I promise I still get through my shifts fine and I make sure to talk to my clients and be pleasant. 

But... well, lately, when I wake up, there's just this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. Like I can still function and do what I need to do, but inside, I just feel really sad and... flat, I guess. 

I know it's probably normal to be a little down after a loss, right? I just hope I'm not overreacting or being too sensitive about it... does that make sense?
Besides feeling sad, have you noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even outside of work?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still try to keep up with my hobbies, you know? I really like gardening, and I've been making sure to get out there and water my plants. I mean, maybe I'm not spending quite as much time out there as I usually do, but I'm still doing it. 

I really try to stay positive and keep busy, so I'm definitely still doing things I enjoy. I hope that's a good sign? Like, that means I'm coping okay, right?
Have you noticed any other physical changes lately, like unusual tiredness, weight gain, feeling unusually cold, or dry skin?

Um, no, my weight is fine, and I don't think my skin is dry or anything like that. I'm taking care of myself, I promise. 

But... well, I guess I have been feeling a little bit tired lately? I don't want it to sound like I'm slacking off at work, because I always make sure my clients are taken care of. It's just... even on days I don't do much, my body feels kind of worn out. Like, simple things, um, like helping a client shower or just carrying my own groceries inside... they just seem to take more out of me than they usually do. 

I'm probably just not sleeping as well since my uncle passed, right? It's normal to be a little tired, isn't it? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm letting it affect my work or anything.
Since your uncle passed away, how has your sleep been—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up much earlier than you'd like?

Um, well... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. I really try to get a full night's rest so I can be sharp for my clients the next day, I always prioritize that. 

But, um... yeah, it's been a little all over the place. Sometimes I just lie there in the dark, and my mind just keeps going over family stuff and everything that's happened. Or, like, I'll wake up way before my alarm is supposed to go off, and I just can't seem to settle back down and fall asleep again. 

I know stress can mess with your sleep a bit, so I'm sure it's just a temporary thing, right? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be. It's pretty normal to have a few restless nights when you're grieving, wouldn't you say?
Have you been feeling unusually worthless or guilty about things, even things that aren't really your fault, since your uncle passed away?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel worthless or anything like that. I know I do good work, and I'm a good person. I always try my best to be there for people, especially my family and my clients. 

But, um... I guess I do feel a little guilty sometimes. Just... about my tío. I keep, you know, replaying things in my head. Like, I think about what I should have done for him before he died. Maybe I should have called him more often, or... or visited him sooner before things got so bad. 

I just... I end up feeling like I kind of failed him, you know? As family. But I know everyone feels a little regret when someone passes, right? It's just a normal part of grieving, I think. I mean, I'm sure I'm not the only one who feels this way, right?
Since your uncle passed away, have you had any thoughts about death in general, or thoughts that you'd be better off not being alive?

Um... oh, no, no, I would never do anything to hurt myself. I want to be really clear about that. I know my clients rely on me, and my family needs me, so I wouldn't... I wouldn't ever do anything like that. 

But, um... I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, and I know this sounds bad... there have been a few mornings lately where I just... I kind of think it wouldn't be the worst thing in the world if I just didn't wake up. 

It's not that I want to die, I promise! It just... it scares me that the thought even crosses my mind, you know? It's probably just because I'm so tired and missing my tío, right? That's a pretty common way to feel when you're grieving and overwhelmed, isn't it? I just... I don't want you to think I'm crazy or unstable or anything.
Since your uncle passed away, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight—eating noticeably more or less than usual?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I always try to make sure I'm eating right so I have enough energy for work. My clients need me to be on my feet and helping them, so I can't afford to, you know, skip meals or anything like that. 

I guess maybe my appetite has been a little... normal? I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently, or stepping on the scale and seeing a big change. I try to keep a pretty steady routine with my meals. 

Sometimes, maybe I don't finish everything on my plate if I'm feeling a bit sad about my tío, but I still eat. That's pretty typical, right? Just a little less hungry when you're going through a tough time? I'm sure I'm doing okay in that department, wouldn't you agree?

Doctor, I think you might have forgotten to ask the next question... I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information, so whatever you need to know, just ask, okay? I'm happy to help however I can.

Has this sadness and fatigue actually affected your ability to perform your daily responsibilities—for example, missing work, making significant errors with clients, or withdrawing from family and friends—beyond just feeling more tired?

Oh, no, definitely not missing work! I always show up. My clients really count on me, so I make sure I'm there no matter what. And I haven't made any big errors or anything like that, I promise. 

I mean... I guess if I'm looking at the really small things... I have been a little bit, um, distracted? But just a little! Lately, I've just been asking my coworkers to sort of double-check my client documentation before I submit it. Just to be completely safe, you know? It's always good to have a second pair of eyes when you're feeling a bit foggy, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a perfect job for them.

And at home... well, my wife is wonderful, and she's sort of taken over paying some of the bills and doing the household scheduling for right now. I'm just not quite as reliable with all those little details at the moment, just with being so tired and everything. But that's a pretty normal way for couples to support each other when one of them is grieving, isn't it? I'm still pulling my weight in other ways, I really am. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything... I'm still handling things okay, don't you think?

patient.answer:
Oh, no, definitely not missing work! I always show up. My clients really count on me, so I make sure I'm there no matter what. And I haven't made any big errors or anything like that, I promise. 

I mean... I guess if I'm looking at the really small things... I have been a little bit, um, distracted? But just a little! Lately, I've just been asking my coworkers to sort of double-check my client documentation before I submit it. Just to be completely safe, you know? It's always good to have a second pair of eyes when you're feeling a bit foggy, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a perfect job for them.

And at home... well, my wife is wonderful, and she's sort of taken over paying some of the bills and doing the household scheduling for right now. I'm just not quite as reliable with all those little details at the moment, just with being so tired and everything. But that's a pretty normal way for couples to support each other when one of them is grieving, isn't it? I'm still pulling my weight in other ways, I really am. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything... I'm still handling things okay, don't you think?

inference.note: Functional impairment (needing coworker double-checks, spouse taking over household tasks) combined with passive suicidal ideation, guilt, sleep disturbance, and fatigue lasting at least 2 weeks now meets full symptom count and duration criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, exceeding what would be expected for uncomplicated grief/adjustment disorder. Ruling out F43.21 given the severity and symptom clustering are more consistent with a major depressive episode than a normal stress response.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary concern or reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 2-week history of depressed mood, anhedonia (partial), fatigue, sleep disturbance (early waking, difficulty maintaining sleep), guilt, passive suicidal ideation, subjective concentration difficulty, and mild functional impairment (needing help double-checking work, spouse taking over household tasks) following bereavement. While onset follows a significant loss, the severity and breadth of symptoms (passive death wishes, pervasive guilt beyond the loss, functional impairment) exceed what is typically expected in uncomplicated bereavement, supporting a diagnosis of a depressive episode rather than normal grief alone. Symptom count meets criteria for a depressive episode (unspecified severity given some symptoms are minimized/downplayed by patient).
